why: Holmes uses this exact name in ¶85 for the woman the bill was made out for.
Holmes says in ¶85 that twenty-two guineas is heavy for a single costume.

text: Who is the Madam Derbyshire of the bill?
why: Holmes's remark about Madam Derbyshire's expensive tastes, on a bill found in Straker's pocket, invites this question. The wording is neutral.

text: Who is the Madam Derbyshire of the bill? — another woman
why: The bill names only William Derbyshire, a supposed friend of Straker's, so the woman's identity is open. It is natural to consider that she is someone other than the obvious candidates.
